designation: REAL footage. Small, hand-built set. Every label states who made it and how reliable it is. No label here was produced by the TraceLine pipeline itself.

provenance_classes.manual: judged by a person (the annotator, an AI engineer working in this repo) looking at decoded frames
provenance_classes.source_label: a clip-level label copied from the dataset's own page or README; not independently verified
provenance_classes.derived: computed from a second recorded signal (e.g. CAN speed) that ships with the clip
provenance_classes.unverified: no check was possible; stated so the number is not over-read

scoring.note: A collision alert is a true positive when its source-time interval overlaps [onset - before, onset + after] of a manually labelled window on the same file. Alerts in clips whose full content was reviewed and that are outside any window are false positives. Alerts in clips with accident_present=true but no located window are reported separately and are NOT counted as true or false positives.

clips.scene: fixed daytime intersection, tram and crossing traffic, 15.1 s, VFR

event_windows.basis: 6 fps crops around the junction: two light cars not touching at 4.75 s, in contact (one car pushed sideways, debris) at 4.92 s. Reviewed whole clip at 1 fps for other collisions: none seen.
event_windows.reliability: single annotator, visual, onset known to about +/-100 ms

clips.note: intersection_demo_share.mp4 is the same footage re-encoded at another size and is not scored separately.

clips.scene: TUMTraf-Accid3nD r09_s01 gantry S050, 10 s window (t=48..58 s), 25 fps

event_windows.basis: 25 fps crops: a yellow car steers toward a white van parked on the shoulder and its front crumples with debris at 3.80-3.84 s; it is against the van's side by 4.0 s. Whole clip reviewed at 1 fps: no other collision.
event_windows.reliability: single annotator, visual, onset known to about +/-50 ms

clips.note: The data-acquisition report said no collision had been found in this window. A collision is in fact visible here; that report's statement is superseded by this label.
Site label: rear-end. The annotator could not locate the impact at 1-6 fps. Alerts here are not scored.
Site label: sideswipe. Two vehicles are already adjacent at the start; impact not located. Alerts here are not scored.
Site label: head-on. At 1 fps two cars sit still at the centre for the entire clip, so it looks like aftermath only; the impact itself is probably not in the clip. Alerts here are not scored.
Site label: single-vehicle. A two-party collision rule does not apply. Alerts here are not scored.
Site label: t-bone. No impact was visible to the annotator at 1 fps. Alerts here are not scored.

clips.note: Frames 3.2-4.4 s at 10 fps show no collision; this view does not include the shoulder where the crash happens. Rest of the clip not reviewed at fine rate.
Reviewed at 1 fps: dense traffic, no collision seen. A brief contact between 1 fps samples cannot be excluded.

clips.scene: ego vehicle yields to a turning car (CAN: 8.3 m/s to 1.85 m/s, about -0.3 g); moving camera, VFR

event_windows.basis: CAN pose speed falls from 8.3 m/s at scene t=5 s to 1.85 m/s at t=8 s (clip t=2..5 s); peak decel about -2.8 to -3.0 m/s2. The data report says it is an ordinary yield, not a collision.

clips.note: Braking without collision: any collision alert here is a false positive.
